text:
alex: quick sanity check — I pulled a user's API_KEY into a .env and curl returns 401. snippet I'm running: `curl -H \"Authorization: Basic $API_KEY\" https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate`

maya: that will only work if $API_KEY is the full base64 of \"username:password\". for our API we usually send `Authorization: Bearer <raw_key>` or Basic with colon + base64.

alex: ah — I thought Basic accepted the raw token. so for basic i need `echo -n \"$API_KEY:\" | base64` ? (empty pwd)

maya: yep. important: use `-n` so echo doesn't append a newline. command: `curl -H \"Authorization: Basic $(echo -n $API_KEY: | base64)\" ...`

sam: also watch out on mac/linux pbcopy/pbpaste adding a newline — i saw this bite us. `echo -n` check or `tr -d '\\n'` when you read from file.

alex: i'm on Windows (pwsh) — what's the idiomatic base64 there without adding extra = padding/newline weirdness?

harini: in PowerShell: `[Convert]::ToBase64String(([Text.Encoding]::Utf8).GetBytes("$env:API_KEY:"))` — then pass that as Basic value. no extra newline.

maya: if you want the easiest fix, use Bearer: `curl -H \"Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY\" ...` and avoid base64. But if some clients expect Basic (legacy), ensure the `:` after key when base64-ing.

sam: quick checklist i send people: 1) Is header `Bearer` vs `Basic`? 2) If Basic, did you base64 \"key:\" (note colon)? 3) Did your env loader include trailing newline or BOM? `xxd` or `cat -A` can help. 4) Powershell vs bash handling.

alex: did `echo -n $API_KEY: | base64` and curl now works. thanks y'all. 

devex-bot: Helpful doc: https://redwood.devex/internal/auth#api-keys (shared for future reference) :thumbsup:

harini: adding: if you're storing keys in systemd unit `EnvironmentFile=`, systemd strips trailing newlines but other runners might not. for k8s secrets, `echo -n` when creating the secret.

alex: will add a short note to sdk README about \"use Bearer or if Basic, base64 key with trailing colon and no newline\" and ping once done. thanks! :raised_hands:
